line: The forty small cards and the sixteen courts, in four suits, through which Crowley carries the ten numbers.

sections.title: Forty small cards in four suits
sections.line: Crowley ties the ten numbers to the small cards and divides those cards into suits by the elements.

quotes.quote: These ten numbers are represented in the Tarot by the forty small cards.
These are divided into four suits according to the four elements.

sections.title: Each number
sections.line: Each number has a significance of its own, in Crowley's account. He gives the number four as an example: it symbolises Law, Restraint, Power, Protection and Stability.

quotes.quote: each number has a significance of its own; each corresponds with all phenomena
It symbolises such ideas as Law, Restraint, Power, Protection and Stability.

sections.title: Suits and elements
sections.line: Crowley gives the four suits their elements in one sentence, and his diagram ties the suits to the four elements.

quotes.quote: “Wands”, attributed to Fire; “Cups”, to Water; “Swords”, to Air;
This diagram shows the attribution of the four Suits of the pack to the four Elements.

sections.title: The Tens and their planets
sections.line: Crowley's text says there is now no planetary attribution for the Tens, but single Tens carry a planet and sign on their own pages. The page keeps both as his statements.

quotes.quote: There is now no planetary attribution to consider.
